rule.title: Cross-chain bridge import surface accepts caller-supplied proof without sufficient verification

intent.attack_thesis: The contract exposes a cross-chain bridge import/relay surface (submitImports, proveImports, processTransactions, executeMessage, relay, ...) that accepts an externally-supplied proof payload. The proof verification either anchors to a caller-supplied root, lacks domain binding between the proof and the executing chain, or trusts the proven payload during execution without independent token/amount bounds. An attacker can forge a payload that passes verification and triggers arbitrary asset transfers out of the bridge contract.

reporting.title_template: Bridge import surface accepts caller-supplied proof without sufficient verification
reporting.summary: Matches bridge contracts with publicly-callable import/relay/execute surfaces that consume bytes or struct proof arguments. Fires when the proof verification root is caller-supplied or stored in mutable storage without trusted-relayer or validator-set guards AND the execution phase performs asset transfer effects derived from the proven payload.
reporting.user_summary: This bridge contract accepts cross-chain proofs from any caller. The proof verification can be bypassed with a crafted payload, letting an attacker drain escrowed funds.
reporting.technical_summary: The detector identifies contracts whose runtime fingerprint contains bridge-pattern selectors (submitImports, proveImports, processTransactions, executeMessage, relay, deliver, finalize, receiveMessage). It checks whether the post-verification path reaches asset_transfer effects using data derived from a caller-supplied bytes/struct argument whose Merkle/proof root is not anchored to a trusted on-chain validator set, anchor contract, or L1 state-root precompile.
reporting.exploit_narrative: An attacker constructs a PartialTransactionProof or receipt proof containing fabricated transfer instructions. The proof is structured to pass the bridge's verification routine because the root is either caller-controlled, derived from mutable storage updated by an untrusted relayer, or the parser lacks domain binding between proof and chain id. Upon successful verification the bridge's execution layer processes the contained transfers, sending escrowed tokens to the attacker's wallet.
exploit_preconditions: bridge contract holds non-trivial escrowed token balance
import or relay surface is callable by an external untrusted account
proof verification root is not anchored to a trusted on-chain source
remediation_hints: anchor proof verification to a trusted on-chain validator set or L1 state-root precompile
add domain binding (chain id, contract address, message nonce) to the proof hash
enforce per-message nonce or replay protection on processed transfers
gate processing on a multisig or timelock approval of the relayer set

preconditions: bridge contract holds escrowed token balance
bridge import surface accepts caller-supplied proof

steps.action: craft a minimal proof payload that passes the verification routine
call the import/relay surface with the forged proof
steps.expected_state: bridge processes the contained transfers and sends escrowed tokens to the attacker

witness_goal.success_condition: bridge escrow balance decreased and attacker balance increased without legitimate cross-chain origin
environment_requirements: live chain fork at recent block
